newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher behind ITC, TELCO rally.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher behind ITC, TELCO rally.

text.p: Share prices closed broadly higher on Friday at Bombay exchanges led by speculative bidding in two top stocks, but the undercurrent was shaky due to an impending increase in oil prices, brokers said.
"The market was led by ITC," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at broker Pashupati Advani. "People are expecting 20-25 percent rise in profits and a bonus issue."
The tobacco conglomerate's board is scheduled to release 1996/97 (April-March) results on Tuesday, but a bonus issue is not on the agenda of the meeting.
The 30-stock Bombay Stock Exchange index ended 18.42 points higher at a provisional 3,759.64.
Shares of Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co (TELCO) were boosted by "no delivery" period, which gave players about four weeks to close accounts against the normal weekly settlements.
TELCO is expected to release 1996/97 results this month.
Tata Iron and Steel Company shares closed 3.5 rupees up at 176.50 after the firm said it will unveil results on May 23.
State-run computer maintenance firm CMC said its net profit fell to 38.4 million rupees in 1996/97 from 126.6 million a year ago.
CMC shares rose 2.25 rupees to 49.25. Analysts said the fall in profits was not because of operational problems but due to a fall in other income to 40.2 million rupees from 297.3 million.
Traders see the market rising after the government raises state-controlled prices of oil, which India imports but sells at below world prices in a complex cross subsidy system.
"Buyers are bidding their time," said Kuntal Shah, chief dealer at broker D.T. Gandhi. "The market will consolidate gains after the (oil) price hike."
